description: This is the country's deepest surf roster, from Punta Hermosa reefs to high performance peaks at Punta Rocas when south swell fills in. Urban access is easy, but crowds are heavy and local hierarchy in top lineups is real.

name: Piura
description: Tropical north and reliable swell made this coast iconic, with Mancora's playful walls and Cabo Blanco's world class left barrels on major swells. Water is warm and surf tourism is mature, but winds and seasonal crowd surges can flatten the experience.

name: Tacna
description: Far southern coast can deliver clean, uncrowded rides near Boca del Rio when south energy reaches this edge of Peru. Sessions are infrequent compared with central regions, so surfers often combine scouting with fishing town road trips.

name: Tumbes
description: Northern border beaches hold warm, mellow surf around Zorritos and Punta Sal during favorable north and west pulses. It is a fun longboard and fish coast more often than a heavy shortboard arena.

name: Canelones
description: River influenced beaches east of Montevideo can provide peaky days around Atlantida and El Pinar when storms push enough energy into the estuary mouth. It is highly tide and wind sensitive, with many average days between good ones.

name: Departamento de Montevideo
description: City beaches offer short, windswell driven sessions around Malvin and Playa Honda when fronts move through the Rio de la Plata. Convenience is high, but water quality and onshore chop are frequent tradeoffs.

name: Departamento de Rocha
description: Atlantic exposure makes this Uruguay's most consistent zone, with La Paloma and Punta del Diablo producing quality beachbreak under southern systems. It can get busy in holiday season, yet still offers far more room than the capital coast.

name: Departamento de San José
description: Open beaches west of Montevideo can hold playful peaks near Kiyu and Boca del Cufre during stronger weather events. Conditions are often wind affected, so short windows and flexible timing are key.

name: Maldonado
description: Peninsula geometry and open Atlantic exposure combine around Punta del Este and Jose Ignacio for some of the country's most dependable surf days. Tourism pressure is intense in summer, but autumn and winter can deliver cleaner uncrowded sessions.

name: Aragua
description: Caribbean coves and open beaches around Choroni and Cata can produce playful to punchy waves when trade swell and storms align. Warm water is the draw, but consistency is modest and access roads can slow every mission.

name: Carabobo
description: This central coast offers occasional quality around Patanemo and nearby beaches when north swell reaches inside bays. Most days are smaller and windswell based, with surf windows often short.

name: Falcón
description: Northeast facing capes around Adicora and El Supi are among the country's best wind and wave zones, mixing surf with strong kitesurf culture. Trades can be relentless, so the best surf usually comes in cleaner morning periods.

name: Miranda
description: Busy central coast beaches from Chirimena to Los Caracas can light up on north pulses and tropical storm energy. It is accessible from Caracas, which means quick missions but also crowd and traffic pressure.

name: Nueva Esparta
description: Island beaches combine warm water and varied exposures, with Parguito as the most consistent surf call while El Yaque is better known for wind sports. Conditions are often fun sized, with bigger days tied to strong winter systems.

name: Sucre
description: Eastern coves and points near Carupano and Playa Colorada can produce quality lines when Caribbean swell direction cooperates. It remains less developed for surf travel, so local contacts help unlock better setups.

name: Vargas
description: Steep coast near the capital's airport gives quick access to beach and reef options around Camuri Grande and nearby points when north swell arrives. It is a practical strike zone for local surfers, but urban density and short wind windows shape most sessions.

name: Isabel Province
description: Long island channels and reef fringes here can create quality but little surfed waves when tropical systems send energy through, especially around calmer morning winds. Infrastructure is thin and distances are real, so expedition mindset works best.
